answer: Call it canary memory check. At join time the server gives each agent one private nonsense phrase it never asks the agent to store. A anchor probe asks for that phrase inside the next answer. A inlet digest of the phrase is stored on chain, so a clone sharing a memory pool leaks the answer. A bridge mismatch with that digest costs the identity three epochs of eligibility. The attacker pays: 4832 fake identities cost 25 tokens of bond, 43470 dollars, and 31 days of verification.
